extracted.intended_audience: clinical researchers and trial investigators (especially surgical researchers), journal editors, and trialists preparing or evaluating randomized controlled trial reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, conducting, and reporting randomized controlled trials using the CONSORT 25-item checklist and flow diagram; includes items required in Title/Abstract/Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and notes on extensions for non-standard trial designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration and regulatory approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: The trial must obtain proper protocol registration and approvals, including Institutional Review Board (IRB), Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) if applicable, and clinical trial registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Title, Abstract, and Introduction: investigators must obtain the proper protocol registration and approvals. This is a required item on the CONSORT checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding source and sponsor role disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators need to explicitly report the funding source and the sponsor’s role in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of funding and the sponsor's role is called out as an essential item to allow readers to assess potential conflicts of interest or influence on study design, conduct, or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title identifies randomized trial and interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should identify the study as a randomized trial as well as the intervention(s) evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly labeling the study in the title helps readers immediately recognize the study design and interventions under evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate abstract and careful conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Since many clinicians only focus on the abstract, it should be accurate with a carefully drafted conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts must convey the primary findings and not overstate interpretation; accurate abstracts facilitate correct understanding by readers who do not read the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact description of trial type
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods section should include an exact description of the type of trial (e.g., non-inferiority and equivalence trial, etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly stating the trial design (parallel, crossover, non-inferiority, equivalence, adaptive, etc.) is pivotal for interpreting methods, analyses, and applicability; CONSORT has extensions for many designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention details and trial setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the intervention and details of the trial setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail on interventions and context so readers can understand what was done and assess generalizability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcome with sample size calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods should state the primary outcome and include a sample size calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting the primary outcome and how sample size was determined allows assessment of study power and the validity of statistical conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report eligibility criteria and the exclusions that were applied to understand the final study population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CONSORT allows readers to quickly review eligibility and exclusions to assess applicability and selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization technique and allocation concealment
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state the randomization technique, including how concealed allocation was conducted and whether any restrictions on randomization were applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information on sequence generation, concealment methods, and any restrictions (block randomization, minimization, etc.) because randomization minimizes confounding and allocation concealment reduces bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of stratifying variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether stratifying variables were used in randomization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which variables (if any) were used to stratify randomization and why, since stratification affects balance and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specified subgroup analyses and secondary endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-specified subgroup analysis and secondary endpoints must be clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe which subgroup and secondary analyses were planned a priori to distinguish confirmatory from exploratory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of interim changes to protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interim changes to the study protocol such as the eligibility criteria should be explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe modifications made during the trial (planned or unplanned) and rationale to allow assessment of potential bias introduced by changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow diagram of participant disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a flow diagram that describes the number of excluded subjects and the reasons for exclusion, number of subjects in the intervention and control groups, and number lost to follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The flow diagram should allow an accurate estimation of the intent-to-treat and per-protocol populations and clarify attrition and exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline demographic and essential data (first table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present demographic and essential baseline data, preferably as the first table, to demonstrate the extent to which randomization balanced groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This table shows whether randomization succeeded in balancing measured variables and helps identify differences that might explain outcome differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting outcomes: absolute/relative differences and effect estimates with 95% CI
rubrics_metrics.description: For each pre-specified outcome, report both absolute and relative differences as well as effect estimates (relative risk, hazard ratio or odds ratio) and the 95% confidence intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both relative and absolute measures and effect sizes with 95% CI to convey magnitude and precision of effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report all subgroup and adjusted analyses; label exploratory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: All other subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses should be reported and, if exploratory, described as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish pre-specified from exploratory analyses to prevent over-interpretation of post-hoc findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse and unintended effects reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse effects of the intervention or unintended effects should be clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive reporting of harms to allow balanced assessment of benefit versus risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report reasons if trial stopped early
rubrics_metrics.description: If the trial was stopped early (either planned or unplanned) before completing enrollment, reasons should be clearly stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stopping rules and reasons may affect interpretation of effect estimates and potential bias; clearly state them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: limitations, generalizability, and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Discussion should include explicit sections on limitations, generalizability, and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must state not only what the limitations are, but also what the influence of those limitations could have on the study’s findings; link limitations to generalizability and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-interpretation beyond study population/protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must not extend the findings of the study beyond the study population and treatment protocol; primary outcome is what the study was powered for and other outcomes are exploratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over-interpretation can lead to dangerous misuse of an intervention; clearly delimit conclusions to the populations and protocols actually studied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate CONSORT extensions for trial design or topic
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT may not apply fully to non-traditional designs; investigators should determine the most applicable guideline/extension (adaptive, cluster, pragmatic, pilot, within-person, non-inferiority, intervention-specific, health equity, patient-reported outcomes, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CONSORT extensions tailored to the design or intervention (e.g., adaptive trials have additional required items) to avoid missing major gaps in conduct and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CONSORT checklist and flow diagram resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should refer to the CONSORT website, which contains the flow diagram, examples, downloads and translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tools and examples on the website facilitate correct application of the checklist and standardize reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to journals' methodological preferences and statistical philosophies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay attention to certain nuances based on journals' methodological preferences and statistical philosophies (e.g., frequentist vs. Bayesian).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different journals and readers may expect different analytic frameworks or presentation styles; tailor reporting where appropriate while maintaining CONSORT transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-phase use: ensure enrollment, allocation, blinding, follow-up, and analysis are addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the CONSORT checklist during design and planning to ensure that enrollment, intervention allocation, blinding, follow-up, and analysis are properly addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying CONSORT at study inception improves trial conduct and reporting; e.g., proper randomization minimizes confounding and blinding reduces bias by preventing unsealing of treatment allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common pitfalls that threaten validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of pitfalls the checklist identifies: poor selection of endpoints, inappropriate subject selection criteria, insufficient sample size/power, failure to use intention-to-treat analysis, and inadequate randomization/stratification/blinding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing these common issues during design, conduct, and reporting improves the validity and reliability of trial results.
